name: rosewater verjuice emulsion
long_description: Whisked almond and verjuice make this pale court sauce lightly opaque, with rosewater leaving a delicate sheen above the sediment.
taste: Sharp green grape is softened by almond body and a restrained floral finish.
smell: It smells of unripe grapes, crushed almonds, and newly distilled rosewater.

name: bitter-orange agrodolce reduction
long_description: Reduced citrus juice, wine vinegar, and sugar form a clear amber sauce whose slow drops cling to the serving spoon.
taste: Bitter orange peel meets bright acidity and dark caramel sweetness in quick succession.
smell: Its fragrance combines scorched sugar, fresh citrus rind, and sharp vinegar.

name: caper-cinnamon court sauce
long_description: Finely minced capers freckle this smooth brown banquet sauce, with cinnamon giving the reduced stock a warmer colour.
taste: Salty caper bite cuts through savoury stock before cinnamon supplies dry warmth.
smell: It carries aromas of brined capers, roasted meat liquor, and cassia bark.

name: raisin-pine-nut court sauce
long_description: Pounded pine nuts thicken a purple-brown raisin reduction, leaving tiny ivory grains suspended in its glossy body.
taste: Fruit sweetness and creamy nuts are checked by sour wine and black pepper.
smell: The sauce smells of soaked raisins, crushed pine kernels, and warming spice.

name: rosemary aqua-vitae cordial
long_description: Fresh rosemary has steeped in a clear distilled cordial, tinting it barely green while a few needles remain below the stopper.
taste: Hot spirit gives way to resinous rosemary, honey, and a dry medicinal close.
smell: Its piercing scent blends clean alcohol, crushed rosemary, and beeswax.

name: citrus-peel aqua-vitae cordial
long_description: Strips of bitter citrus peel colour this refined aqua vitae pale gold, with aromatic oil forming fleeting rings on top.
taste: The cordial burns warmly, then releases orange zest, lemon bitterness, and slight sweetness.
smell: It smells sharply of distilled spirit and freshly pared citrus skin.

name: sage-and-honey cordial spirit
long_description: Honey gives this sage-steeped spirit an amber cast and a heavier pour than unflavoured aqua vitae.
taste: Alcoholic heat carries earthy sage and meadow honey into a long herbal finish.
smell: A heady vapour of spirit, dried sage, and warm honey rises from it.

name: Ottoman rose-petal sherbet
long_description: A clarified petal infusion gives this chilled sherbet a faint blush, with no fragments left in the crystalline drink.
taste: Cool floral sweetness is balanced by lemonlike acidity and a clean watery finish.
smell: It has the perfume of fresh damask roses, sugar, and citrus peel.

name: Ottoman sour-cherry sherbet
long_description: Pressed sour cherries colour this palace sherbet a brilliant ruby, while dilution keeps it clear and freely pouring.
taste: Tart cherry leads decisively before sugar rounds the fruit and softens its astringency.
smell: The drink smells of crushed red cherries and a little fragrant blossom water.

name: Safavid mint sekanjabin concentrate
long_description: Honey, vinegar, and mint have reduced to a translucent green-amber concentrate with a slow syrupy thread.
taste: Sweetness and vinegar strike together, followed by cooling mint and herbal sharpness.
smell: Its concentrated aroma joins honeycomb, wine vinegar, and bruised mint leaves.

name: Mughal saffron-almond sharbat
long_description: Finely strained almonds make this sharbat creamy, while saffron stains it gold and leaves occasional crimson threads.
taste: Nutty richness supports saffron, cardamom, and gentle sugar without becoming cloying.
smell: It smells of almond meal, haylike saffron, green cardamom, and rose.

name: Mughal sandalwood-rose sharbat
long_description: Rose infusion gives this clear court sharbat a pale pink hue, with sandalwood contributing no visible sediment after straining.
taste: Floral rose opens the taste before cool woody spice and light sweetness emerge.
smell: A refined scent of rose petals, damp sandalwood, and sugar hangs over the cup.

name: Ottoman cardamom coffee liquor
long_description: Very finely ground coffee clouds this small black serving, with pale foam and cardamom specks gathering at the rim.
taste: Intense roast bitterness is lifted by green cardamom and a fleeting caramel note.
smell: Its powerful aroma combines fresh coffee grounds, cardamom pod, and hot metal.

name: Ming smoked-plum tea liquor
long_description: Tea and smoked plum produce a clear reddish-brown infusion, with a single wrinkled fruit sometimes left in the pot.
taste: Tannic leaf, tart plum, and hearth smoke create a dry and refreshing flavour.
smell: Steam brings the scents of dark tea, singed plum skin, and charcoal.

name: Ming chrysanthemum tea liquor
long_description: Whole chrysanthemum petals tint this refined infusion clear gold, drifting open like small flowers near the surface.
taste: It tastes lightly floral and grassy, with subtle bitterness and a cooling finish.
smell: The vapour is delicate, recalling dried chrysanthemum heads and spring hay.

name: Japanese whisked tea liquor
long_description: Powdered tea has been whisked into an opaque jade-green liquor capped by a close layer of tiny bubbles.
taste: Concentrated green tea tastes grassy, creamy, and briskly bitter with lasting umami.
smell: It gives off a vivid scent of ground tea leaf, fresh grass, and warm ceramic.

name: Joseon five-flavour berry punch
long_description: Steeped magnolia berries make this court punch a luminous crimson, with pine nuts floating sparsely across the top.
taste: Sweet, sour, bitter, salty, and pungent impressions unfold over a bright berry core.
smell: Its unusual bouquet suggests red berries, pine kernel, and faint cinnamon bark.

name: Ming fermented-black-bean cooking liquor
long_description: Rinsed fermented beans cloud this dark cooking liquid, leaving black fragments and a slight oily lustre behind.
taste: It is intensely salty and savoury, carrying fermented bean depth and mild garlic.
smell: The strong smell recalls aged black beans, brine, and a warm wok.

name: Japanese iri-zake cooking liquor
long_description: Reduced rice wine, dried plum, and fish shaving make this clear amber seasoning liquor delicately glossy.
taste: Dry rice wine supports sour plum and marine savour with restrained salt.
smell: It smells of heated sake, preserved plum, and clean dried fish.

name: achiote-red cacao drink
long_description: Ground cacao and achiote form a red-brown drink with persistent foam and fine dark sediment under the froth.
taste: Bitter cacao is earthy and dry, with peppery achiote and almost no sweetness.
smell: Its scent blends roasted cacao, annatto seed, maize, and aromatic flowers.

name: chile-maize cacao froth
long_description: Maize thickens this dark cacao drink beneath a coarse foam, while red chile flecks remain visible in the cup.
taste: Roasted bitterness and grain body are followed by a clean, rising chile heat.
smell: It smells of ground cacao, toasted maize, dried chile, and smoke.

name: vanilla-flower cacao liquor
long_description: A tall cap of tan foam crowns this dark cacao preparation, perfumed with vanilla orchid and other fragrant flowers.
taste: Cacao remains dry and bitter beneath rounded vanilla and a delicate floral sweetness.
smell: The rich aroma carries roasted beans, vanilla pod, and freshly gathered blossoms.

name: colonial anise-quinoa chicha
long_description: Fermented quinoa gives this early colonial drink a cloudy straw colour, while introduced anise seed dots the loose surface foam.
taste: Mild sourness and grainy nuttiness lead into an aromatic liquorice-like finish.
smell: It smells of wet quinoa, active fermentation, anise, and cool earthen jars.

name: Atlantic maize-millet beer
long_description: Newly arrived maize ferments beside millet in this contact-zone beer, whose ochre sediment gathers beneath a thin pale foam.
taste: Sweet maize lightens the earthy millet and finishes with mild fermented bitterness.
smell: Its aroma brings damp grain, fresh yeast, faint smoke, and calabash.

name: Canary sack cooking wine
long_description: This fortified island wine is deep amber and brilliantly clear, pouring with more weight than an ordinary table vintage.
taste: Ripe grape sweetness, oxidation, and warming alcohol finish on dried fruit and nuts.
smell: It smells richly of sun-dried grapes, old wood, orange peel, and spirit.
